req.title: Logout clears session
req.statement: The system shall clear the session and redirect to / on GET /auth/logout.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /auth/logout must clear the session and redirect to / with a 302 status. I design: (1) a positive test confirming a logged-in user is redirected to '/' with status 302 and session cleared (STC — logged-in → logged-out state transition); (2) a negative test confirming that even an unauthenticated (no session) user hitting /auth/logout still gets 302 to '/' and no server error (NEG — no prior session); (3) a boundary test confirming the redirect Location is exactly '/' and not any other path, and that 'user_id' is absent from the session after logout (BVA — exact redirect target and session key removal). Each test is self-contained with its own app/client/db setup.

tests.name: test_logout_authenticated_user_redirects_302_and_clears_session
preconditions: App is created in TESTING mode with a fresh temp database
Database is initialised with schema and fixture data (user id=1, username='test', password='test')
User 'test' is logged in via POST /auth/login (session contains user_id)
actions: POST /auth/login with username='test' and password='test' to establish session
expected: Subsequent GET / does not show authenticated user (session cleared)
Session no longer contains 'user_id' key after logout
trace: R-FLASKR-011: logout clears session and redirects to / with 302
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in first
login_resp = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert login_resp.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {login_resp.status_code}'

# Verify session has user_id before logout
with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' in sess
    assert sess['user_id'] == 1

# Perform logout
logout_resp = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert logout_resp.status_code == 302
assert logout_resp.headers['Location'] == '/'

# Verify session is cleared after logout
with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_logout_redirect_target_is_exactly_root_not_other_path
preconditions: App is created in TESTING mode with a fresh temp database
Database is initialised with schema and fixture data
User 'test' is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: Inspect Location header for exact value '/'
Follow the redirect and confirm the final page is the blog index (HTTP 200)
expected: Location header equals exactly '/' (not '/auth/login', not '/auth/logout', not '')
Session user_id is absent after logout (exact key check)
trace: R-FLASKR-011: redirect target must be exactly '/', boundary on redirect destination string
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in
login_resp = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert login_resp.status_code == 302

# Logout — do NOT follow redirect
logout_resp = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert logout_resp.status_code == 302

location = logout_resp.headers['Location']
assert location == '/', f'Expected Location="/" but got "{location}"'
assert location != '/auth/login'
assert location != '/auth/logout'
assert location != ''

# Follow redirect manually
index_resp = client.get('/')
assert index_resp.status_code == 200

# Session must not contain user_id
with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess
    assert len([k for k in sess if k == 'user_id']) == 0

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_logout_session_user_id_absent_after_multiple_logouts
preconditions: App is created in TESTING mode with a fresh temp database
Database is initialised with schema and fixture data
expected: Session has no user_id after first logout
Session has no user_id after second logout (idempotent)
trace: R-FLASKR-011: session.clear() is idempotent; repeated logout must not error

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in
login_resp = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert login_resp.status_code == 302

# First logout
resp1 = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert resp1.status_code == 302
assert resp1.headers['Location'] == '/'

with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess

# Second logout (idempotency)
resp2 = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert resp2.status_code == 302
assert resp2.headers['Location'] == '/'

with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_logout_does_not_redirect_to_login_or_5xx
preconditions: App is created in TESTING mode with a fresh temp database
Database is initialised with schema and fixture data
User 'other' (id=2) is logged in via POST /auth/login
expected: Status code is exactly 302 (not 200, not 401, not 403, not 500)
Session cleared: user_id not in session
trace: R-FLASKR-011: any authenticated user (not just id=1) must be logged out correctly; DT covers second user row
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in as 'other' (id=2)
login_resp = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'other', 'password': 'other'})
assert login_resp.status_code == 302

with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert sess.get('user_id') == 2

# Logout
logout_resp = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert logout_resp.status_code == 302
assert logout_resp.status_code != 200
assert logout_resp.status_code != 500
assert logout_resp.headers['Location'] == '/'
assert logout_resp.headers['Location'] != '/auth/login'

with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess

os.unlink(path)
